- When sentiment shows strong negative spikes (e.g., -1.98 or -0.51 recurring), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If model forecasts a sharp upward move after recent high sentiment, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below prior 30-day high.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., 0.96+), model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 10–15% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 10+ consecutive days of high prices; apply 3–5 day decay filter to smooth out overfitting.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.96, -0.51, +0.94), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
